official.deadline_note: No dates are published for the scholarship call itself: Esade states that 'Calls for these scholarship applications are generic and targeted at all those who meet the legally established criteria.' The operative calendar is the rolling admissions cycle for the September 2027 intake, with nine staged deadlines from 30 September 2026 to 30 June 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 intake (September 2027 start) - rolling admissions with nine staged deadlines from 30 September 2026 to 30 June 2027
official.status_note: Esade presents the Scholarship Program as an ongoing annual programme, and the current MBA and MSc application calendar for the September 2027 intake is open (1st deadline 30 September 2026, then 18 November 2026, 13 January 2027, 17 February 2027, 17 March 2027, 21 April 2027, 12 May 2027, 2 June 2027 and 30 June 2027). Esade warns that 'scholarship funds normally run out before the final deadline', although funds are reserved to last throughout the entire process.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published wording for the MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships: 'The amount of these scholarships covers between 50% and 85% of their tuition fees.' The same page frames the programme as a whole: 'Our scholarships cover between 60% to 100% of their tuition fees, and we also offer grants to help them with their room and board' - the 60-100% band belongs to the undergraduate Degree Talent Scholarships, which run for the entire undergraduate or double-degree programme.
benefits: MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships: 'The amount of these scholarships covers between 50% and 85% of their tuition fees.'
Esade Lodging Grants: available for students who live outside Barcelona province and have distinguished academic records though limited financial resources.
Esade Living Grants: aim to help students with solid academic backgrounds and limited resources cover their transportation costs and general expenses.
Esade Exchange Scholarships: an extension of the Esade Talent Scholarships for students who have been given a spot in an exchange programme.

Esade SUD Scholarships: an extension of the Esade Talent Scholarships for students applying to carry out a professional, solidarity-based internship through Esade's University Development Service (SUD) in developing countries.
The Esade Income Share Agreement, supported by the European Investment Fund, can be combined with scholarships or awards.
eligibility: Admission to an official Esade MBA or MSc programme - 'These scholarships are for students to complete official MBA and MSc programs.'
'Candidates with demonstrated talent and financial need are encouraged to apply.'
Meets the legally established criteria of the applicable call ('legally established criteria').
Programme admission: a bachelor's degree or equivalent entitling the holder to postgraduate study in the degree-granting country.
Programme admission (MBA only): a minimum of two years' full-time professional experience post-graduation.
requirements: 'Financial assistance is open to all applicants' and Esade encourages candidates 'to apply when submitting your initial MSc Program application' / 'when you initially apply for a place on the MBA Program'.
'Our Talent Attraction Committee will study their applications to confirm that candidates meet the established requirements.'
Programme admission: fluency in English evidenced by an accepted certificate, or an exemption via native-speaker status or a degree taught in English.
Programme admission: a high score in the Esade Admissions Test (TAE), GMAT or GRE - 'All applicants must take the Esade Admission Test (TAE), GMAT or GRE.'
Two recommendation letters submitted as part of the application process, from professional and/or academic referees.
documents: Online application form (Esade Admissions Portal) with the non-refundable EUR 150 application fee paid and the electronic signature completed.
CV and a scan of the identity card (Spanish citizens) or passport (EU and non-EU nationals).
Bachelor transcripts and bachelor's degree/diploma, in the original language, with official translations into Catalan, Spanish or English where needed.
English test score report (official TOEFL sent directly by ETS; IELTS and Cambridge certificates as originals or certified true copies) or the diploma supplement proving the language of instruction.
Esade Admissions Test result, or unofficial GMAT/GRE scores uploaded plus official scores sent to Esade (GRE code 5761; GMAT codes vary by MSc, 93M-3K-60 for the MBA).
Supporting economic documents evidencing household financial need - the specific list is not enumerated on the published Scholarship Program or fees pages.
selection_criteria: Demonstrated talent ('talented students with excellent academic track records from diverse socio-economic backgrounds').
Demonstrated financial need - the award is for 'students with outstanding academic track records but whose financial situations may represent an obstacle for them'.
Confirmation by the Talent Attraction Committee that candidates meet the established requirements.

Programme-level assessment by the Admissions Committee of academic performance, admissions test score, professional experience (MBA), essays and recommendations, with a mandatory interview for selected applicants.
coverage: Tuition fees: between 50% and 85% of the tuition fee of the official Esade MSc programme or MBA ('The amount of these scholarships covers between 50% and 85% of their tuition fees').

Room and board: not part of the Talent Scholarship amount. Esade publishes separate complements - Lodging Grants for students living outside Barcelona province and Living Grants for transportation costs and general expenses.

Exchange and solidarity internships: Esade Exchange Scholarships and Esade SUD Scholarships extend the Talent Scholarship to students placed on an exchange programme or on a SUD solidarity internship.
Living costs, flights and travel are not funded by the Talent Scholarship itself; the GBP/Global Master's programme fees note likewise states that 'flights and meals are not included'.
application_method: MSc: submit the online application form and apply for financial aid at the same time - 'We encourage you to apply when submitting your initial MSc Program application.'
MBA: 'If you are thinking of applying for an award, we urge you to do so when you initially apply for a place on the MBA Program.'

The file is then reviewed by the Admissions Team, an interview is held if required, and the Admissions Committee and Scholarship/Talent Attraction Committee assess the application, with the decision visible in the Student Portal.
Award applications for Esade's graduate prizes are started by logging into the Admissions Portal and accessing the Award Information section (one award per candidate).
official.application_route: One online application in the Esade Admissions Portal (esade.my.site.com) that doubles as the financial-aid request, followed by document validation, an interview if required, and a joint admissions and Scholarship Committee decision.
official.study_mode: Full-time (Esade states that, with the exception of internships, students are expected to dedicate themselves full-time to their studies)
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship or residency restriction is published for the MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships: the call is 'generic and targeted at all those who meet the legally established criteria', and Esade states that 'Financial assistance is open to all applicants'.
official.international_eligibility: Yes. No nationality restriction is published for the MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships, and Esade states that financial assistance is open to all applicants. Related external awards listed on Esade's pages are more restrictive - for example the Fundacio Princesa de Girona scholarships target Spanish citizens or residents.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to candidates admitted to an official Esade MBA (Full Time) or MSc programme in Management. No donor-specific programme restriction is published for the MSc/MBA Talent Scholarships, unlike the undergraduate Dedicated Talent Scholarships where companies may specify the applicable programme (BBA, Bachelor in Law, BITLASI or double-degree programmes) or the student profile.
official.duration: Full Time MBA: 12 months, with the option to complete in 12, 15 or 18 months. Esade MSc programmes in Management: one-year programmes. Global Master's: two-year programmes.
official.description: Esade's Scholarship Program offers talented students with excellent academic track records from diverse socio-economic backgrounds the opportunity to study at Esade, funded by donations from companies, foundations, alumni and the Esade community. The MSc and MBA Talent Scholarships support students completing official Esade MBA and MSc programmes who demonstrate both talent and financial need, and are possible thanks to the generosity of the Esade community.
official.region: Spain (Esade campuses in Barcelona and Madrid)
official.program_type: Merit- and need-based tuition scholarship for Esade's official MSc programmes in Management and Full Time MBA, with separate room-and-board, exchange and solidarity-internship grant complements
official.english_requirement: Programme-level requirement published for both the MSc programmes and the Full Time MBA: TOEFL iBT 100 (new scale 5.0, minimum 4.5 in each section), IELTS Academic 7.0, Certificate in Advanced English B+, Certificate of Proficiency in English C+, Academic Pearson 68+ or Duolingo English Test 130+. Certificates must be no more than two years old. Native English speakers, and candidates whose bachelor's degree (at least 120 ECTS) or master's degree (60 ECTS) was taught entirely in English, are exempt on production of a diploma supplement or university certificate stating the language of instruction. No scholarship-specific English requirement is published.

verification.notes: Verified live on 10 October 2026 against the Esade Scholarship Program page (English and Spanish editions), the Scholarship Program and Financial Aid overview, the Financial Aid index, and the MSc and Full Time MBA fees-and-financing and admissions pages. The 50%-85% tuition range and the 'generic call' wording for the MSc/MBA Talent Scholarships are published verbatim on the Scholarship Program page. The graduate fees pages foreground Esade Excellence Awards (10%-50% of MSc tuition, 26% average in the last intake) alongside the need-based line and state that awards are not compatible with other Esade prizes. Programme-wide key facts on the English Scholarship Program page (5M EUR dedicated, 295 scholarship recipients, 84% of recipients' tuition fees covered, 8.4% of undergraduate students) differ slightly from the Spanish edition of the same page (5M EUR, 267 recipients, 87% average coverage, 7.2% of degree students).

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition-discount line, not a full ride: it removes 50-85% of your Esade MSc or Full Time MBA fee and leaves everything else on you. Ask for financial aid in the same session in which you submit the programme application, because Esade assesses both together and the money visibly drains as the rounds progress. Come with hard evidence of household finances, since demonstrated need carries as much weight here as talent, and expect the mandatory interview before a final decision lands.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants with a strong academic record and genuine, documentable financial need who are targeting an official Esade MSc in Management or the Full Time MBA, including international candidates who can evidence household income.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the online application in the Esade Admissions Portal and request financial aid in the same sitting - Esade explicitly tells applicants to apply for aid with the initial programme application.
Sit the Esade Admissions Test, GMAT or GRE early and aim at or above the published class averages (around GMAT 615 in the current edition, GRE 160/162).
Book IELTS 7.0 Academic or TOEFL iBT 100 well before the round you target; certificates older than two years are refused and official TOEFL scores must be sent by ETS.
Prepare translated, certified household income evidence before your target round, because the need file is what separates this line from the merit-only Excellence Awards.
Budget the residual before you apply: on the EUR 39,000 one-year MSc fee, a 50% award still leaves roughly EUR 19,500 to fund, plus the EUR 150 application fee, materials, visa and living costs.
Line up two referees and enter their details in the form early, since the automatic request goes out only after that section is saved.
common_rejection_risks: Applying in a late round after the scholarship pot for that intake has been consumed - Esade states that scholarship funds normally run out before the final deadline.
Holding or requesting a second Esade prize: awards are not compatible with each other, so stacking the Talent line with an Excellence Award fails.
An incomplete file: Esade only considers an application complete once the online form, the paid application fee and all manually validated documents are in.
Recommendation letters or referee details left blank, which stalls validation and pushes your file into a weaker round.
On the MBA side, falling short of the two years of post-graduation professional experience that is a hard admissions requirement.
Assuming the need assessment can be postponed: the Committee decides on the evidence submitted with the application.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond the discounted tuition slice: 15-50% of the fee that the award does not cover (roughly EUR 5,850 to EUR 19,500 on the EUR 39,000 one-year MSc tuition, or roughly EUR 12,375 to EUR 41,250 on the EUR 82,500 Full Time MBA fee), plus the EUR 150 application fee, the EUR 100 MBA Student Association fee, study materials, flights and meals (excluded even from Global Master's programme fees), visa, translation and legalisation costs, and living costs - Esade quotes approximately EUR 1,200 a month for a shared flat with food and transport in Barcelona.
document_audit: Transcripts and diplomas issued in any language other than Catalan, Spanish or English need an official translation, or the Admissions Team will not validate them.
Only official TOEFL scores sent directly by ETS are accepted (institution code 0507 for the MSc, 0884 for the MBA); IELTS and Cambridge certificates must be originals or certified true copies.
The English certificate has a two-year shelf life, and the medium-of-instruction exemption needs a diploma supplement that explicitly states the language of instruction.
Need evidence is household-based, so expect to document family income rather than only your own finances.
GMAT/GRE unofficial scores go into the portal while the official report must be requested from the test provider using Esade's codes, including the programme-specific GMAT code for each MSc.
alerts: The scholarship call publishes no dates of its own; the only public calendar is the rolling admissions cycle (30 September 2026 to 30 June 2027), and Esade warns the money usually runs out before the last deadline.
You can hold one Esade award only, so choose deliberately between the need-based Talent line and the Excellence Awards (10%-50% of MSc tuition, 26% average in the last intake).
If you live outside Barcelona province, ask about the separate Lodging and Living Grants - they are the only published help with rent, transport and general expenses.
Non-EU applicants should start visa paperwork immediately, since Spanish rules from May 2025 require the student visa application at least 60 days before the programme begins.
A scholarship decision follows admission rather than replacing it, so an applicant who is not admitted has nothing to discount.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One online application in the Esade Admissions Portal doubles as the financial-aid request; the file is validated, an interview is held if required, and the Admissions and Scholarship Committees issue a single decision in the portal, with about a month elapsing from a complete file to the verdict.
